loop: gauntlet: a builder and a separate critic with fresh context per piece. The critic runs ours next to native, names the biggest gap, and the piece loops until the critic picks ours.

items.title: #1 dedup ratio on the real worktree corpus
items.detail: Full run on 45 slots, 843,889 files, 273.43 GiB raw, 0 errors. Raw 1.00x, per-file zstd 3.60x, whole-file dedup 3.12x, CDC only 5.08x, CDC + zstd 14.04x. A median extra lumen slot costs 0.47 GiB compressed (4.9% of raw). Caveat: 97.5% of raw is cargo target/ and 91.7% is one repo, so 14x is a Rust build-output result. Write-up: docs/spikes/1-dedup-corpus.md. Gate met.

items.title: #7 block store (merged)
items.detail: Merged to main (c1619ec) after five rounds. Round-4 findings fixed with regression tests at fce19f9 and re-verified by me: main merged, scope clean (store, store doc, lockfile), CI green on both platforms, 131 crate tests pass, fmt and clippy clean. Fixed: torn newest SYNCED slot plus valid checkpoint no longer reports clean (32-offset tear sweep, 0 clean reports); restore-after-acknowledge; acknowledgements carry real nonce and claimed id; close and Drop share one idempotent finish; pack ids reserved durably before create; marker durable before any truncate; lock cause PROVED: flock lives on the open file description, a bare fork keeps the store locked, 50 ms Instant deadline plus holder pid in the error; nested records not resurrected when the outer header still checksums. 23 mutants: 22 killed, 1 by build failure, 0 survivors. 4000-case crash and 1800-case power-loss models 0 lost, 0 wrong. LIMITS (documented): operator restore of old files and a nested record under a failed outer CRC are best-effort; salvage costs seconds per MiB (1 MiB read amplification not removed); throughput A/B unmeasurable at load 100-300, NO throughput claim; legacy high-water bytes sit outside the watermark CRC. Not independently re-run by me: the 4000-case crash model and the VM runs (builder figures).

items.title: #10 garbage collection
items.detail: Round-1 critic findings fixed (builder, head 6b654e2) and re-verified by me: main merged, scope clean, ci.yml untouched, CI green on both platforms, fmt/clippy clean, 243 gc+store tests pass. F1 per-root mark attribution, F2 barrier held only in step 5, F3 forget_pack on early returns, F4 crash-ordering tests now run in plain cargo test. items.title: #11 Linux FUSE adapter (merged)
items.detail: Merged to main (48645b9). Round-2 critic blockers fixed with regression tests and re-verified by me at 0af5b6b: main merged, scope clean, CI green on both platforms, Mac 45 tests, Linux VM mount suite 48 unit + 40 mount + 11 regress, builder ran it 10 times with 0 failures and no leftover mounts. Fixes: create + failed open no longer leaks the file; an empty non-eof readdir page is retried then fails loudly; a held descriptor sees a rewrite behind the mount (page revalidator, default on); ordering claim corrected to the Vfs concurrency contract (#41); wedged lane reported by health(). New: the shared conformance suite now runs through the mount (129 run, 1 fails identically on the VM's own filesystem), and it found and fixed a real defect (a removed-but-referenced directory reported nlink 2 instead of 0). Not covered by CI until the Linux FUSE job lands (PR in progress). Decision recorded: shared mode keeps the 1 s attr cache; long timeouts only after the daemon wires the Invalidator.

items.title: #12 macOS NFS loopback mount (merged)
items.detail: Merged to main. Round-2 critic blockers fixed with regression tests and re-verified by me at 8ea2c80 (main merged, CI green on both platforms, scope clean, 138 crate tests pass, builder reports ignored mount suite 19/19 and 37/37 mutants killed). Adopted the frozen trait: Retry maps to NFS3ERR_JUKEBOX, unknown Error variants are a logged SERVERFAULT, unknown FileKind is never served as a regular file, exhaustiveness guard test, root COMMIT is the whole-mount barrier. SHIPS WITH AppleDoubleMode::Hide as default; Translate is opt-in. Follow-up issue filed for a round-3 review of Translate and the new security code before flipping the default or releasing. Not tested with a second uid; a dead server still hangs ls for 20 s+ on macOS 26 (cure: signal cleanup and sweep, which the daemon must call).

items.detail: New. items.title: #56 daemon on the real core backend (merged)
items.detail: Builder done (head 9b2d62a), CI green. Core is now the default daemon backend: clone = fork_snapshot, reset = promote_base, rename = rename_snapshot; a store with unacknowledged damage is refused at open. ctl gained mount_snapshot and unmount_snapshot with the holder check under the framework's per-snapshot lock (issue #51 items 1-2). Two real daemon bugs found by the end-to-end run and fixed: expect_no_holders scanned the store instead of the mount; the store lock released at drop instead of in order. 5 real-mount e2e tests: all pass on Linux FUSE; on macOS NFS 2 FAIL on #53. Smoke (VM, FUSE, 2% scale, 1 rep, load1 0.07): g4 0.003 to 0.345 s, g5 write 5792 to 46 MiB/s, g6 9 ms to 511 ms: tiny corpus, treat as a first look only. MERGED at c4187ef after the builder removed the committed smoke artifacts (verified: no progress/ files in the diff, no store binaries), merged main, and documented that macOS NFS on core is broken until #53. My checks: scope clean, CI green on both platforms, fmt/clippy clean, 124 daemon+ctl tests pass. Not independently re-run: the 5 real-mount e2e tests and the smoke numbers.

items.title: #53 P0: core alias release vs stateless NFS handles
items.detail: Found by the daemon e2e. A directory created through the macOS NFS mount goes Stale seconds later: cowfs-nfs forgets the Ino right after handing it out (stateless), core then releases the virtual alias at commit and the number changes. Reproduces in core alone. Core builder making the Ino stable for the session (retained compact alias map, bounded, documented cap) on branch v1/core-alias, with real-mount proof against PR #56's two failing e2e tests. FUSE keeps its own table; checking whether it has the same window.
